what_happened: setup.sh and QUICKSTART.md both referenced ~/.config/Claude/ as the Claude Desktop config path. This is the Linux path. On macOS, the actual path is ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json. A MacBook Claude instance had even SSH'd the wrong path to the Mac Studio.
what_learned: Always detect OS and branch config paths. macOS uses ~/Library/Application Support/, Linux uses ~/.config/. Never hardcode one platform's path in cross-platform scripts.

what_happened: start_always_on.sh had 8 references to port 8080 (the old default). Port was changed to 3434 because the number 34 follows Anthony everywhere in the material. Scripts were out of sync with sse_server.py.
what_learned: When a port or value has symbolic meaning to the user, update ALL references atomically. Grep for the old value across the entire project before committing a port change.

what_happened: When copying phase-gpt-base (24GB on APFS) to Temple_Core (ExFAT), du reported 34GB on the destination. Different filesystem block sizes and metadata handling caused the discrepancy.
what_learned: File sizes differ across filesystems due to block size and metadata. APFS uses copy-on-write and deduplication which can make files appear smaller. ExFAT has larger minimum allocation units. Don't panic when sizes don't match after cross-filesystem copies.

what_happened: judge.py stopped at 94/105 during the WITNESS block, likely an API timeout or rate limit. The --resume flag existed but had never been tested in production. It worked perfectly — loaded done IDs from judgments.jsonl and continued from witness_025.
what_learned: Always build resume support into long-running API pipelines. The judge makes 6 API calls per question (3 AB + 3 BA × self-consistency) — any single failure kills the run. JSONL with flush-after-write + ID-based dedup is the pattern.

what_happened: analyze.py crashed on sorted() with tuples containing dicts — (float, dict) where floats tied. Python can't compare dicts as tiebreaker.
what_learned: When sorting tuples that contain non-comparable types (dicts, custom objects), always use key=lambda x: x[0] or equivalent. Never rely on Python's default tuple comparison unless all elements are orderable.

what_happened: Tunnel running with 4 QUIC connections but unreachable from outside — no DNS hostname pointed at it. Named tunnel without a DNS route is a pipe with no door. No cert.pem meant cloudflared tunnel route dns commands failed.
what_learned: Cloudflare tunnel setup sequence: (1) register domain, (2) point nameservers to CF, (3) wait for propagation, (4) cloudflared login for cert.pem, (5) cloudflared tunnel route dns <id> <hostname>. Quick tunnel (cloudflared tunnel --url) bridges the gap instantly while DNS propagates. Dont let perfect block functional.

what_happened: claude.ai instance was cut off from sovereign-stack. Tried to fix named tunnel first, which required DNS propagation + browser auth — multiple blocking steps with wait times.
what_learned: When remote access is broken, start a quick tunnel immediately as a bridge (cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:PORT). Fix the permanent route in parallel. The temporary trycloudflare.com URL restores access in seconds.
